| `Spread` | Random neighbor displacement for scatter effect (always uses frame access) |
| `Turbulence` | Fractal noise displacement using value noise with octave summation (always uses frame access) |
| `Twirl` | Spiral rotation decreasing from center to edge (always uses frame access) |
| `Wave` | Independent X/Y sinusoidal displacement with configurable amplitude and wavelength (always uses frame access) |
| `Wind` | Directional pixel streaks at bright edges simulating wind (always uses frame access) |
| `Bulge` | Radial bulge/pinch power-law distortion from center (always uses frame access) |
| `Dents` | Noise-based surface dent displacement distortion (always uses frame access) |
| `OceanRipple` | Dual-axis sinusoidal ocean ripple distortion (always uses frame access) |
| `Offset` | Wrap-around pixel offset displacement (always uses frame access) |
| `Shear` | Linear horizontal or vertical shear displacement (always uses frame access) |
| `ZigZag` | Radial zigzag sinusoidal displacement from center (always uses frame access) |
| [`Fisheye`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisheye_lens) | Equidistant fisheye lens projection (180° FOV) — radial barrel distortion with configurable strength (always uses frame access) |

#### Noise

| Filter | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `AddNoise` | Deterministic positional hash noise, monochromatic or per-channel (always uses frame access) |
| `Despeckle` | Hybrid median filter combining horizontal, vertical, and diagonal medians (always uses frame access) |
| `DustAndScratches` | Replace outlier pixels with neighborhood median (always uses frame access) |
| `Mezzotint` | Random dot pattern where density matches luminance (always uses frame access) |
| `ReduceNoise` | Non-local means approximation weighting neighbors by color similarity (always uses frame access) |
| `Diffuse` | Random positional hash displacement noise (always uses frame access) |

#### Render

| Filter | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `Clouds` | Procedural multi-octave value noise clouds blended with source (always uses frame access) |
| `DifferenceClouds` | Difference blend of procedural noise with source image (always uses frame access) |
| `Fibers` | Vertical fiber texture with noise modulation blended with source (always uses frame access) |
| `PlasmaTexture` | Multi-octave plasma noise with per-channel phase offset (always uses frame access) |
| `Supernova` | Radial starburst light rays with spoke pattern added to source (always uses frame access) |

#### Morphology

| Filter | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `BottomHat` | Black bottom-hat: closing minus original highlights dark details (always uses frame access) |
| `Closing` | Morphological closing: dilation then erosion (always uses frame access) |
| `Opening` | Morphological opening: erosion then dilation (always uses frame access) |
| `TopHat` | White top-hat: original minus opening highlights bright details (always uses frame access) |

### Filter Discovery

```csharp
using Hawkynt.ColorProcessing.Filtering;

// Enumerate all available filters
foreach (var filter in FilterRegistry.All)
  Console.WriteLine($"{filter.Name} ({filter.Category})");

// Find by name or category
var vonKries = FilterRegistry.FindByName("VonKries");
var analysisFilters = FilterRegistry.GetByCategory(FilterCategory.Analysis);

// Apply via descriptor (reflection-based, useful for UI/tooling)
var desc = FilterRegistry.FindByName("Blur");
using var result = desc.Apply(source);
```

## Blend Modes

The library provides 27 blend modes for compositing bitmaps, covering all standard categories from image editing applications. Blend modes operate on normalized [0,1] float channel values and support alpha compositing with adjustable strength.

### Usage

```csharp
using Hawkynt.ColorProcessing.Blending.BlendModes;
using Hawkynt.Drawing;

using var background = new Bitmap("base.png");
using var overlay = new Bitmap("overlay.png");

// Blend with specific mode — returns new bitmap
using var multiplied = background.BlendWith<Multiply>(overlay);
using var screened = background.BlendWith<Screen>(overlay, 0.5f);  // 50% strength

// In-place blending — modifies background directly
background.BlendInto<Overlay>(overlay);

// Blend filter result with adjustable opacity
using var softGlow = source.BlendWith(new GaussianBlur(3, 3), 0.4f);  // Normal blend
using var sharpened = source.BlendWith<Screen, UnsharpMask>(new UnsharpMask(1.5f, 0.05f), 0.7f);

// HSL component modes
using var recolored = background.BlendWith<HueBlend>(overlay);
using var luminosity = background.BlendWith<LuminosityBlend>(overlay);
```

### Available Blend Modes

#### Normal

| Mode | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `Normal` | Replaces background with foreground |

#### Darken

| Mode | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `Multiply` | Multiplies channels, darkening the image |
| `ColorBurn` | Darkens by dividing inverted background by foreground |
| `Darken` | Takes the darker of two channels |
| `LinearBurn` | Adds channels and subtracts 1, darkening the image |

#### Lighten

| Mode | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `Screen` | Inverts, multiplies, and inverts again, lightening the image |
| `ColorDodge` | Brightens by dividing background by inverted foreground |
| `Lighten` | Takes the lighter of two channels |
| `Add` | Adds channels, clamping at 1 |
| `LinearDodge` | Adds channels, clamping at 1 (alias of Add) |

#### Contrast

| Mode | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `Overlay` | Combines Multiply and Screen based on background luminance |
| `SoftLight` | Soft contrast adjustment using W3C formula |
| `HardLight` | Overlay with foreground and background swapped |
| `VividLight` | Combines Color Burn and Color Dodge based on foreground |
| `LinearLight` | Combines Linear Burn and Linear Dodge based on foreground |
| `PinLight` | Replaces dark or light halves based on foreground |
| `HardMix` | Posterizes to black or white based on channel sum |

#### Inversion

| Mode | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `Difference` | Absolute difference between channels |
| `Exclusion` | Similar to Difference but with lower contrast |
| `Subtract` | Subtracts foreground from background, clamping at 0 |
| `Divide` | Divides background by foreground |

#### Component (HSL-based)

| Mode | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `HueBlend` | Takes hue from foreground, saturation and lightness from background |
| `SaturationBlend` | Takes saturation from foreground, hue and lightness from background |
| `ColorBlend` | Takes hue and saturation from foreground, lightness from background |
| `LuminosityBlend` | Takes lightness from foreground, hue and saturation from background |

#### Other

| Mode | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `GrainExtract` | Extracts film grain texture from the image |
| `GrainMerge` | Merges film grain texture back into the image |

### Blend Mode Discovery

```csharp
using Hawkynt.ColorProcessing.Blending;

// Enumerate all available blend modes
foreach (var mode in BlendModeRegistry.All)
  Console.WriteLine($"{mode.Name} ({mode.Category})");

// Find by name or category
var multiply = BlendModeRegistry.FindByName("Multiply");
var darkenModes = BlendModeRegistry.GetByCategory(BlendModeCategory.Darken);
```

## Frequency Domain

The library provides FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) and DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform) operations for frequency-domain image analysis and manipulation.

### Types

| Type | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `Complex` | Lightweight complex number (`float Real, float Imaginary`) with arithmetic operators, magnitude, phase, conjugate, and polar conversion |
| `Fft1D` | 1D FFT using Cooley-Tukey radix-2 algorithm (in-place, power-of-2 length) |
| `Fft2D` | 2D FFT via row-wise then column-wise 1D FFT |
| `Dct1D` | 1D Discrete Cosine Transform (Type-II forward, Type-III inverse) |
| `Dct2D` | 2D DCT via row-wise then column-wise 1D DCT |

### Bitmap Extension Methods

```csharp
using Hawkynt.ColorProcessing.FrequencyDomain;
using Hawkynt.Drawing;

// FFT operations
var spectrum = source.ToFrequencyDomain();           // Bitmap → Complex[,] (grayscale FFT)
using var reconstructed = BitmapFrequencyDomainExtensions
    .FromFrequencyDomain(spectrum, width, height);   // Complex[,] → Bitmap

// Spectrum visualization
using var magnitude = source.GetMagnitudeSpectrum(); // Log-scaled magnitude (zero-freq centered)
using var phase = source.GetPhaseSpectrum();         // Phase spectrum visualization

// DCT operations
var coefficients = source.ToDctDomain();             // Bitmap → float[,] (grayscale DCT)
using var fromDct = BitmapFrequencyDomainExtensions
    .FromDctDomain(coefficients, width, height);     // float[,] → Bitmap
```

## Known Issues

- **Bedi resampler**: Produces out-of-range color values on some inputs, causing `IndexOutOfRangeException` in the sRGB gamma LUT. Tests skip gracefully when this occurs.

#### `BayerMatrix`

Generates Bayer threshold matrices for ordered dithering and other spatial threshold applications. A Bayer matrix of size `N` contains the values `0..N*N-1` arranged so that iterated halving of the space maximises dispersion — the defining property that makes it useful for dithering, anti-aliasing patterns, stochastic sampling and similar tasks.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Generate` | `static float[,] Generate(int size)` | Generates a Bayer threshold matrix of the specified size. |
| `IsValidSize` | `static bool IsValidSize(int size)` | Tests whether `size` is an acceptable Bayer matrix size (positive power of two). |

| `FindNearestBatchNoCache` | `void FindNearestBatchNoCache(ReadOnlySpan<TWork> colors, Span<int> outIndices)` | Batched nearest-palette lookup. For each colour in `colors`, writes the corresponding palette index to `outIndices` at the same offset. Falls through to per-pixel `FindNearestNoCache` for cube cells / metrics that don't benefit from cross-pixel SIMD; uses `FindMinDistanceBatch` when the metric implements it AND the lookup has no cube (so all pixels query the same candidate set = the full palette), which is the K-means-style worst case the SSE2 path was built for. |

Intended for hot paths where the input colour is effectively unique per call (e.g. the per-pixel adjusted colour inside error diffusion) so the cache adds overhead instead of amortising work. |

#### `SpaceFillingCurves`

Pure utility generators for 2D space-filling-curve traversal orders. Given a rectangular region, each method returns the pixel coordinates in the order dictated by the curve — useful for dithering, imaging, low-discrepancy sampling, cache-friendly pixel access, and compression.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MaxHilbertOrder` | `const int MaxHilbertOrder` | Largest Hilbert order we accept (2^7 = 128 covers most real images). |
| `MaxPeanoOrder` | `const int MaxPeanoOrder` | Largest Peano order we accept (3^5 = 243 covers most real images). |
| `Hilbert` | `static List<ValueTuple<int, int>> Hilbert(int width, int height, int startY = 0, int? order = null)` | Generates a Hilbert-curve traversal of a `width` × `height` region starting at row `startY`. |

| `Peano` | `static List<ValueTuple<int, int>> Peano(int width, int height, int startY = 0, int? order = null)` | Generates a Peano-curve traversal of a `width` × `height` region starting at row `startY`. |

#### `BlendModeCategory`

Categorizes the type of blend mode.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Normal` | `0` | Normal compositing modes. |
| `Darken` | `1` | Darkening blend modes (Multiply, ColorBurn, Darken, LinearBurn). |
| `Lighten` | `2` | Lightening blend modes (Screen, ColorDodge, Lighten, Add, LinearDodge). |
| `Contrast` | `3` | Contrast blend modes (Overlay, SoftLight, HardLight, VividLight, LinearLight, PinLight, HardMix). |
| `Inversion` | `4` | Inversion blend modes (Difference, Exclusion, Subtract, Divide). |
| `Component` | `5` | HSL component blend modes (Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity). |
| `Other` | `6` | Other blend modes (GrainExtract, GrainMerge). |

#### `ColorConverter`

Generic color converter for extracting luminance and RGB components from arbitrary color spaces.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FromNormalizedRgb` | `static TWork FromNormalizedRgb<TWork>(float r, float g, float b)` | Creates a TWork color from normalized RGB components with full opacity. |
| `FromNormalizedRgba` | `static TWork FromNormalizedRgba<TWork>(float r, float g, float b, float a)` | Creates a TWork color from normalized RGBA components. |
| `GetAlpha` | `static float GetAlpha<TWork>(in TWork color)` | Gets the alpha component from a color (1.0 if not available). |
| `GetLinearRgb` | `static LinearRgbF GetLinearRgb<TWork>(in TWork color)` | Converts a working color to LinearRgbF. |
| `GetLinearRgba` | `static LinearRgbaF GetLinearRgba<TWork>(in TWork color)` | Converts a working color to LinearRgbaF. |
| `GetLuminanceInt4B` | `static byte GetLuminanceInt4B<TWork>(in TWork color)` | Gets the BT.601 luminance of a 4-component byte color using pure integer arithmetic. |
| `GetLuminanceInt` | `static byte GetLuminanceInt(byte r, byte g, byte b)` | Gets the BT.601 luminance of a color using pure integer arithmetic. |
| `GetLuminanceInt` | `static byte GetLuminanceInt<TWork>(in TWork color)` | Gets the BT.601 luminance of a 3-component byte color using pure integer arithmetic. |
| `GetLuminance` | `static float GetLuminance<TWork>(in TWork color, bool highQuality = false)` | Gets the luminance of a color in the range 0.0-1.0. |
| `GetNormalizedRgb` | `static ValueTuple<float, float, float> GetNormalizedRgb<TWork>(in TWork color)` | Gets normalized RGB components (0.0-1.0 range) from a color. |
| `GetNormalizedRgba` | `static ValueTuple<float, float, float, float> GetNormalizedRgba<TWork>(in TWork color)` | Gets normalized RGBA components (0.0-1.0 range) from a color. |
| `LuminanceFromRgb` | `static float LuminanceFromRgb(float r, float g, float b)` | BT.601 luminance from already-normalised RGB channels — for filter kernels that have decomposed RGB via `GetNormalizedRgb` / `GetNormalizedRgba` and don't have the original color struct handy. Replaces the duplicated `ColorMatrices.BT601_R * r + ColorMatrices.BT601_G * g + ColorMatrices.BT601_B * b` pattern that was scattered across ~30 filter files before Round 22. |
| `Saturate` | `static float Saturate(float x)` | Saturate (clamp to `[0, 1]`) a single float channel value. Replaces the duplicated `Math.Min(1f, Math.Max(0f, x))` pattern. |

#### `AdaptiveDitherer`

Adaptive dithering system that automatically selects the best dithering algorithm based on image characteristics analysis.

Implements `IDitherer`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AdaptiveDitherer` | `AdaptiveDitherer(AdaptiveStrategy strategy = 3)` | Creates an adaptive ditherer with the specified strategy. |
| `Balanced` | `static AdaptiveDitherer Balanced { get; }` | Pre-configured instance with balanced settings. |
| `PerformanceOptimized` | `static AdaptiveDitherer PerformanceOptimized { get; }` | Pre-configured instance optimized for performance. |
| `QualityOptimized` | `static AdaptiveDitherer QualityOptimized { get; }` | Pre-configured instance optimized for quality. |
| `RequiresSequentialProcessing` | `bool RequiresSequentialProcessing { get; }` |  |
| `SmartSelection` | `static AdaptiveDitherer SmartSelection { get; }` | Pre-configured instance using smart algorithm selection. |
| `Dither` | `void Dither<TWork, TMetric>(TWork* source, byte* indices, int width, int height, int sourceStride, int targetStride, int startY, in TMetric metric, TWork[] palette)` |  |

#### `AdaptiveDitherer.AdaptiveStrategy`

Strategy for selecting the dithering algorithm.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |

| `Balanced` | `1` | Balance quality and performance. |
| `PerformanceOptimized` | `2` | Prioritize performance over quality. |
| `SmartSelection` | `3` | Use smart scoring to select optimal algorithm. |

#### `AdaptiveVarianceDiffusionDitherer`

Adaptive-variance error-diffusion ditherer — per-pixel weight matrix that interpolates between Floyd-Steinberg (low local variance, flat regions) and Atkinson (high local variance, textured regions) to keep edges sharp while flat areas still dither smoothly.

Implements `IDitherer`.

#### `AnalyticFourierScreenDitherer`

Ordered ditherer whose 16×16 threshold matrix is built by specifying a target 2-D Fourier power spectrum — an annular high-pass with explicitly-tuned DC-notch width and cutoff slope — and ranking cells by an analytic score that approximates the inverse-Fourier synthesis of that spectrum. The result is a dispersed-dot screen whose residual error energy sits in a tuned frequency band rather than the broad sweep of generic blue-noise.

Implements `IDitherer`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Instance` | `static AnalyticFourierScreenDitherer Instance { get; }` | Default instance. |
| `RequiresSequentialProcessing` | `bool RequiresSequentialProcessing { get; }` |  |
| `Dither` | `void Dither<TWork, TMetric>(TWork* source, byte* indices, int width, int height, int sourceStride, int targetStride, int startY, in TMetric metric, TWork[] palette)` |  |

#### `ContentStrategy`

Specifies the content type for adaptive dithering strategy selection.

| `ExtremeLuminance` | `3` | For very dark or very bright regions - special handling. |
| `Balanced` | `4` | Balanced approach for mixed content. |

#### `DitheringStrategy`

Different dithering strategies for different types of image content.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `StructurePreserving` | `0` | Preserve structural edges and boundaries. |
| `SmoothGradient` | `1` | Optimize for smooth gradient transitions. |
| `DetailEnhancing` | `2` | Enhance fine details in textured regions. |
| `ExtremeLuminance` | `3` | Handle very dark or very bright regions. |
| `Balanced` | `4` | Balanced approach for typical content. |

#### `DitheringType`

Defines the type/category of a dithering algorithm.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `0` | No dithering - nearest neighbor quantization only. |
| `Ordered` | `1` | Ordered dithering using threshold matrices (e.g., Bayer patterns). |
| `ErrorDiffusion` | `2` | Error diffusion dithering (e.g., Floyd-Steinberg, Atkinson). |
| `Noise` | `3` | Blue noise dithering using void-and-cluster patterns. |
| `Random` | `4` | Random/noise-based dithering. |
| `Custom` | `5` |  |

#### `NoiseMode`

Selects how the noise value drives the per-pixel palette decision.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ThresholdSelection` | `0` | Noise picks between nearest and second-nearest palette colors based on a threshold derived from how far the source sits between them. Default; avoids clamping-at-edges and preserves palette fidelity. (Classic blue-noise-style dithering.) |
| `AdditivePerturb` | `1` | Noise is added to the source color before nearest-neighbor lookup, producing a more "random grain" look similar to analog film noise. Simpler algorithm, often preferred for posterization effects and retro aesthetics. |

#### `NoiseType`

Defines the type of noise used for dithering.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `White` | `0` | White noise: uniform random distribution with equal energy at all frequencies. |
| `Blue` | `1` | Blue noise: high-frequency emphasis, reduced low-frequency content. Produces even spatial distribution. |
| `Pink` | `2` | Pink noise (1/f): equal energy per octave, reduced high-frequency content. More natural-looking than white noise. |
| `Brown` | `3` | Brown/Red noise (1/f²): strong low-frequency emphasis (Brownian motion). Smooth, organic appearance. |
| `Violet` | `4` | Violet noise (f): high-frequency emphasis, opposite of pink. Sharp, textured appearance. |
| `Grey` | `5` | Grey noise: perceptually uniform noise adjusted for human vision response. |

#### `SpaceFillingCurve`

Types of space-filling curves for image traversal.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Hilbert` | `0` | Hilbert curve - subdivides space into 4 quadrants recursively. Order range: 1-7. Each order doubles the resolution (order n covers 2^n × 2^n). |
| `Peano` | `1` | Peano curve - subdivides space into 9 parts recursively (3×3 grid). Order range: 1-5. Each order triples the resolution (order n covers 3^n × 3^n). |
| `Linear` | `2` | Simple serpentine (boustrophedon) scan - alternating left-to-right and right-to-left rows. No order parameter needed. |

#### `StippleDitherer`

Ordered dithering using a pre-placed Poisson-disc stipple pattern — dots are added to the screen in an order that maximises the minimum inter-dot distance, so the resulting threshold matrix has stipple-art aesthetics rather than halftone or Bayer grid structure.

Implements `IDitherer`.

#### `AccentedEdges`

Accented edges filter -- Sobel-based edge detection with brightness and smoothness modulation. Computes Sobel gradient magnitude, scales by edge width, applies smoothness blending with an averaged neighborhood, and modulates the result by brightness. The original image is blended with the detected edge color based on edge magnitude.

Implements `IFrameFilter`, `IPixelFilter`.

#### `Clahe`

Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (Karel Zuiderveld 1994). Splits the image into a regular grid of `tileSize`×`tileSize` tiles, computes a clipped per-tile histogram CDF, then bilinearly interpolates between neighbouring tile CDFs to remap each pixel's luminance — preserving local contrast while suppressing the over-amplification of noise that plain histogram equalization produces in flat regions.

Implements `IFrameFilter`, `IPixelFilter`.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `Clahe` | `Clahe()` |  |
| `Clahe` | `Clahe(int tileSize = 8, float clipLimit = 4)` |  |
| `Default` | `static Clahe Default { get; }` |  |

| `InvokeFrameKernel` | `TResult InvokeFrameKernel<TWork, TKey, TPixel, TDecode, TProject, TEncode, TResult>(IResampleKernelCallback<TWork, TKey, TPixel, TDecode, TProject, TEncode, TResult> callback, int sourceWidth, int sourceHeight)` |  |

Stops must be sorted by position ascending; the first stop's position must be 0 and the last stop's position must be 1; at least two stops are required. #### `Lottes`

Lottes single-curve filmic tone-mapping (Timothy Lottes 2016 GDC). Generic four-parameter rational curve `f(x) = x^a / (x^(a·d)·b + c)` where (b, c) are pre-computed from (midIn, midOut) and (hdrMax, hdrOut) constraints so the curve hits both anchors exactly.

Implements `IPixelFilter`.

#### `Mantiuk`

Mantiuk 2006 perceptual gradient-domain tone mapping with per-pixel gradient attenuation. The 4-neighbour log-luminance gradients at each output pixel are damped by a contrast-attenuation function `α(|G|)`; the centre log-luminance is reconstructed as a Jacobi step of the Poisson integration of the attenuated gradient field. Multi-pass application drives the result toward the global Poisson solution.

Implements `IFrameFilter`, `IMultiPassFilter`, `IPixelFilter`.

#### `Reinhard`

Reinhard tone mapping operator (Reinhard, Stark, Shirley & Ferwerda 2002). Implements the global luminance compressor `L_out = L_in / (1 + L_in)` — the simplest of the Reinhard family — applied uniformly to all pixels in the luminance domain, then redistributed back to RGB by per-pixel scaling.

Implements `IPixelFilter`.

#### `ReinhardExtended`

Reinhard extended tone mapping operator with explicit white-point control (Reinhard, Stark, Shirley & Ferwerda 2002, eq. 4). Maps `L_out = L * (1 + L / W²) / (1 + L)` where `W` is the smallest luminance to be mapped to 1.0 — values at or above `W` burn out cleanly.

Implements `IPixelFilter`.

#### `FillSpec`

How a geometric transform fills pixels whose inverse-mapped source coordinate lies outside the source image.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FillSpec` | `FillSpec(GeometricFillMode mode, Color color)` | Creates a fill specification. |
| `Clamp` | `static FillSpec Clamp { get; }` | Edge-replicate (clamp to nearest edge). |
| `Color` | `Color Color { get; }` | The constant fill colour for `Constant`. |
| `Mirror` | `static FillSpec Mirror { get; }` | Mirror across the source boundary. |
| `Mode` | `GeometricFillMode Mode { get; }` | The boundary policy. |
| `Transparent` | `static FillSpec Transparent { get; }` | Out-of-bounds pixels are written transparent. |
| `Wrap` | `static FillSpec Wrap { get; }` | Tile (wrap modulo source dimensions). |
| `Of` | `static FillSpec Of(Color color)` | Out-of-bounds pixels are written with the supplied opaque colour. |

#### `GeometricFillMode`

Selects how an inverse-mapped destination pixel that falls outside the source image is filled.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Constant` | `0` | Fill out-of-bounds pixels with a fixed colour (see `Color`). Default is transparent. |
| `Clamp` | `1` | Clamp the source coordinate to the nearest valid edge pixel (a.k.a. "extend" / "edge-replicate"). Yields no visible seam at corners. |
| `Wrap` | `2` | Wrap the source coordinate modulo the source dimensions. Useful for tileable textures. |
| `Mirror` | `3` | Mirror the source coordinate across the boundary. Avoids hard seams without the obvious tiling that `Wrap` can introduce. |

#### `GeometricInterpolation`

Selects which separable resampling kernel a geometric transform uses when an inverse-mapped destination pixel falls between source samples.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NearestNeighbor` | `0` | Nearest-neighbour. Fastest. Pixel-exact for 90° rotations and integer translations. |
| `Bilinear` | `1` | 2×2 bilinear interpolation. Default for arbitrary-angle warps. |
| `Bicubic` | `2` | 4×4 Mitchell-style bicubic. Sharper than bilinear with mild ringing. |
| `Lanczos3` | `3` | 6×6 Lanczos-3 windowed sinc. Highest quality, slowest. |

#### `Lut3D`

A 3D color look-up table — three-dimensional grid of RGB samples used as the canonical primitive for color grading, gamut mapping, technical LUTs, and "look" application in film / video pipelines. Sampling is performed with either trilinear or tetrahedral interpolation.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Lut3D` | `Lut3D(int size, float[] data, ValueTuple<float, float, float>? domainMin = null, ValueTuple<float, float, float>? domainMax = null)` | Creates a new 3D LUT. |
| `Data` | `float[] Data { get; }` | Flat sample storage. Length = `Size`³ · 3. |
| `DomainMax` | `ValueTuple<float, float, float> DomainMax { get; }` | Domain maximum applied per channel (default 1). |
| `DomainMin` | `ValueTuple<float, float, float> DomainMin { get; }` | Domain minimum applied per channel (default 0). |
| `Size` | `int Size { get; }` | Size of each axis (e.g. 33 for a typical "33×33×33" grading LUT). |
| `Identity` | `static Lut3D Identity(int size = 17)` | Returns the identity LUT of the given size (output equals input — no transform). Useful as a base for testing or for procedural LUT construction. |
| `Sample` | `ValueTuple<float, float, float> Sample(float r, float g, float b, Lut3DInterpolation interpolation = 1)` | Samples the LUT at the given normalised input color using the requested interpolation. |

Result is sorted ascending by distance; ties resolve to first-occurrence order. The default implementation (provided via `FindNClosestScalar`) is a partial selection sort (O(N·k)); SIMD overrides may vectorise for small `k`. |

#### `GaussianPyramid`

Burt-Adelson Gaussian pyramid: a sequence of progressively half-sized Gaussian-blurred copies of the source image.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Build` | `static Bitmap[] Build(Bitmap source, int levels)` | Builds a Gaussian pyramid from `source` with `levels` total levels (level 0 = original size, level k = source / 2^k). |
| `ExpandOnce` | `static Bitmap ExpandOnce(Bitmap source, int targetWidth, int targetHeight)` | Performs one 2× upsample + Gaussian smoothing step (the "expand" operation). Used by `LaplacianPyramid` reconstruction; exposed so callers can build their own pyramid-walking traversals. |
| `ReduceOnce` | `static Bitmap ReduceOnce(Bitmap source)` | Performs one Gaussian-blur + 2× downsample step. Public so callers can build custom-shaped pyramids if needed (e.g., wavelet-style steerable pyramids). |

#### `LaplacianPyramid`

Burt-Adelson Laplacian pyramid: the band-pass decomposition of an image into a sequence of difference-of-Gaussians plus the coarsest Gaussian residual.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LevelCount` | `int LevelCount { get; }` | Total number of pyramid levels (including the coarsest Gaussian residual). |
| `Build` | `static LaplacianPyramid Build(Bitmap source, int levels)` | Builds a Laplacian pyramid from `source`. |
| `HeightAt` | `int HeightAt(int level)` | Height of pyramid level `level`. |
| `Reconstruct` | `Bitmap Reconstruct()` | Reconstructs the source bitmap from this pyramid. Lossless in floating-point arithmetic; final encoding into 8-bit BGRA clamps to [0, 255] with rounding. |
| `RoundTripMaxDelta` | `static int RoundTripMaxDelta(Bitmap source, int levels)` | Round-trip helper for tests / external diagnostics: build, then reconstruct, returning the difference image (max abs ΔRGBA per pixel). |

#### `DeltaERms`

Root-mean-square of CIE ΔE2000 (CIEDE2000) over all pixels. Provides a perceptual-uniform color difference metric suitable for color reproduction quality assessment.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Compute` | `static double Compute(Bitmap reference, Bitmap candidate)` | Returns RMS ΔE2000. |
| `DeltaEMax` | `static double DeltaEMax(Bitmap reference, Bitmap candidate)` | Returns the worst (max) ΔE2000 across all pixels. |

#### `Fsim`

Feature Similarity Index (Zhang, Zhang, Mou & Zhang 2011). Combines a Phase Congruency feature map and a Gradient Magnitude map under a phase-congruency-weighted average to score perceptual similarity.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Compute` | `static double Compute(Bitmap reference, Bitmap candidate)` | Computes Feature Similarity between two same-size bitmaps. |

#### `MsSsim`

Multi-Scale SSIM (Wang, Simoncelli & Bovik 2003) — applies SSIM at successive 2× downsampled scales and combines them with empirically tuned exponents `α=(0.0448, 0.2856, 0.3001, 0.2363, 0.1333)`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Compute` | `static double Compute(Bitmap reference, Bitmap candidate)` | Computes MS-SSIM with a default 8-pixel window per scale. |
| `Compute` | `static double Compute(Bitmap reference, Bitmap candidate, int windowSize)` | Computes MS-SSIM with a configurable per-scale window size. |

#### `Psnr`

Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) — measures the ratio between the maximum possible pixel value (255 for 8-bit) and the RMS reconstruction error, expressed in decibels.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Compute` | `static double Compute(Bitmap reference, Bitmap candidate)` | Computes PSNR between two same-size bitmaps over R, G, B channels. |

#### `Ssim`

Structural Similarity Index (Wang, Bovik, Sheikh & Simoncelli 2004). Combines luminance, contrast and structure terms over local windows; values in `[-1..1]` with 1 = perfect similarity, 0 = no structural correlation.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Compute` | `static double Compute(Bitmap reference, Bitmap candidate)` | Computes the mean SSIM over `reference` vs `candidate` on luminance. |
| `Compute` | `static double Compute(Bitmap reference, Bitmap candidate, int windowSize)` | Computes mean SSIM with a configurable window size (must be ≥ 2). |

#### `QuantizationType`

Defines the type/category of a color quantization algorithm.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Tree` | `0` | Tree-based quantization (e.g., Octree). |
| `Clustering` | `1` | Clustering-based quantization (e.g., K-Means). |
| `Splitting` | `2` | Splitting-based quantization (e.g., Median Cut, Wu). |
| `Fixed` | `3` | Fixed palette quantization. |
| `Variance` | `4` | Variance-based quantization. |
| `Neural` | `5` | Neural network-based quantization (e.g., NeuQuant). |
| `Preprocessing` | `6` | Preprocessing wrapper that modifies input before passing to inner quantizer. |
| `Postprocessing` | `7` | Postprocessing wrapper that refines output from inner quantizer. |

#### `QuantizerAttribute`

Attribute to provide metadata for color quantization algorithm implementations.

| `DisplayName` | `string DisplayName { get; set; }` | Gets or sets the display name for UI purposes. |

#### `ResampleKernelHelpers`

Helpers shared by every separable resampler kernel to compute the destination-pixel region where the whole sample window falls inside the source image. The pipeline then splits the outer loop into 4 edge bands + 1 safe interior and dispatches the interior to an OOB-free inner loop — zero per-pixel branch, ready for SIMD vectorisation.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ComputeSafeDestinationRegion` | `static Rectangle ComputeSafeDestinationRegion(int kxMin, int kxMaxExcl, float scaleX, float offsetX, int sourceWidth, int targetWidth, int kyMin, int kyMaxExcl, float scaleY, float offsetY, int sourceHeight, int targetHeight)` | Computes the destination-pixel rectangle where a kernel with sample window `[x0 + kxMin, x0 + kxMaxExcl)` × `[y0 + kyMin, y0 + kyMaxExcl)` (with `x0 = floor(destX * scaleX + offsetX)`) is guaranteed to sample only in-bounds source pixels. |
| `ComputeSafeDestinationRegion` | `static Rectangle ComputeSafeDestinationRegion(int radius, float scaleX, float offsetX, int sourceWidth, int targetWidth, float scaleY, float offsetY, int sourceHeight, int targetHeight)` | Convenience overload for the `[-r+1, r+1)` window family used by every separable resampler in this library except NearestNeighbor (0,1) and Bilinear/Hermite/Cosine/Smoothstep (0,2). |

#### `ScalerCategory`

Categorizes a resizing algorithm by the fidelity axis: how faithfully the output reflects the source, and what scaling grammar applies.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Rescaler` | `0` | Pattern-matched fixed integer scale (upscale/downscale): HQ, XBR, XBRz, Eagle, Scale2x, SuperXbr, NNEDI3, … |
| `Resampler` | `1` | Deterministic, source-faithful arbitrary-scale (upsample/downsample): kernel convolution (Lanczos, Bicubic, Mitchell-Netravali, …), vector tracing (Kopf-Lischinski), edge-directed interpolation (DCCI, EEDI2), seam carving. |
| `Regenerator` | `2` | Regenerative (learned/neural) arbitrary-scale. Synthesises pixels via a model — may hallucinate detail that diverges from the source. AI super-resolution, diffusion upscalers. |

#### `BilateralVariant`

Bilateral filter variants.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Standard` | `0` | Standard settings - balanced smoothing and edge preservation. |
| `Soft` | `1` | Soft settings - more smoothing, larger spatial sigma. |
| `Sharp` | `2` | Sharp settings - sharper edges, smaller range sigma. |

#### `CrtCaligari`

Stylistic CRT-style upscale inspired by Caligari's CRT shader. NOT a port of the shader — the spot-weight `(1-r²)²` per-axis blend is NOT implemented; this filter uses fixed darkening percentages over each scaled block.

#### `HqMode`

Specifies the filtering mode for HQ/LQ scalers.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Normal` | `0` | Standard YUV-based color comparison mode. Uses original HQ algorithm thresholds. |
| `Bold` | `1` | Brightness-weighted edge detection mode (SNES9x style). Adds contrast-based filtering for stronger edges on high-contrast boundaries. |
| `Smart` | `2` | Automatic mode that switches between Normal and Bold based on corner analysis. Uses Bold mode when no corners match the center pixel. |

#### `HqQuality`

Specifies the quality level for HQ/LQ scalers.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `High` | `0` | High quality mode with full interpolation patterns. |
| `Low` | `1` | Low quality mode with simplified interpolation. Faster but produces less smooth results. |

#### `SmaaQuality`

SMAA quality presets.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Low` | `0` | Low quality - conservative edge detection, less smoothing. |
| `Standard` | `1` | Standard quality - balanced edge detection and smoothing. |
| `High` | `2` | High quality - sensitive edge detection, more smoothing. |
| `Ultra` | `3` | Ultra quality - maximum smoothing for best quality. |

#### `BitmapGaussianBlurIntExtensions`

Integer-only Gaussian blur via three iterated `BoxBlurInt` passes. Three box passes approximate a true Gaussian to within ~3% RMS error (Wells 1986; Kovesi 2010 "Fast Almost-Gaussian Filtering"). Combines the 50×+ speedup of the int sliding-window box with a near-Gaussian frequency response.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `GaussianBlurInt` | `static Bitmap GaussianBlurInt(this Bitmap @this, double sigma)` |  |

Integer-only Median filter with constant per-pixel cost regardless of kernel radius, using the Perreault–Hébert 2007 sliding-histogram algorithm ("Median Filtering in Constant Time", IEEE TIP 16(9), 2007).

#### `BitmapMorphologyIntExtensions`

Integer-only morphological operations: `ErodeInt` (per-channel min over a square kernel) and `DilateInt` (per-channel max). Uses Lemire's monotonic-deque sliding-window algorithm — O(1) amortised per pixel regardless of radius, far faster than per-pixel kernel scanning. Pure int byte arithmetic.

#### `FastResampleMode`

Fast integer-only resampling kernels for the Bgra8888 fast path.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NearestNeighbor` | `0` | Nearest-neighbor sampling. No interpolation; preserves hard edges. |
| `Bilinear` | `1` | Bilinear interpolation over a 2x2 source neighborhood. Q16 fractional weights. |
| `Box` | `2` | Area-average (box). Integrates fractional source pixel coverage with Q24 weights. |

#### `ColorMetric`

Selectable runtime color-distance metric for tools that pick by name (CLI, config files). Each value can be turned into a `Func` via `AsFunc`, or invoked directly with `Calculate`.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Euclidean` | `0` | Squared Euclidean distance over R,G,B,A channels. |
| `EuclideanRgbOnly` | `1` | Squared Euclidean distance over R,G,B only (alpha ignored). |
| `EuclideanBT709` | `2` | Squared Euclidean distance with BT.709 luma weights (R,G,B = 2126,7152,722). |
| `EuclideanNommyde` | `3` | Squared Euclidean distance with Nommyde-tuned weights (R,G,B = 4984,8625,2979). |
| `WeightedEuclideanLowRed` | `4` | Weighted squared Euclidean favoring green/blue over red (R,G,B = 2,4,3). |
| `WeightedEuclideanHighRed` | `5` | Weighted squared Euclidean favoring red/green over blue (R,G,B = 3,4,2). |
| `Manhattan` | `6` | Manhattan (L1) distance over R,G,B,A channels. |
| `ManhattanRgbOnly` | `7` | Manhattan distance over R,G,B only (alpha ignored). |
| `ManhattanBT709` | `8` | Manhattan distance with BT.709 luma weights. |
| `ManhattanNommyde` | `9` | Manhattan distance with Nommyde-tuned weights. |
| `WeightedManhattanLowRed` | `10` | Manhattan distance favoring green/blue over red. |
| `WeightedManhattanHighRed` | `11` | Manhattan distance favoring red/green over blue. |
| `CompuPhase` | `12` | CompuPhase low-cost color metric (https://www.compuphase.com/cmetric.htm). |
| `PngQuant` | `13` | PNGQuant alpha-aware difference (white-point weighted). |
| `WeightedYuv` | `14` | Weighted distance in YUV space (luminance preferred). |
| `WeightedYCbCr` | `15` | Weighted distance in YCbCr space. |
| `Cie94Textiles` | `16` | CIE94 with textile-industry coefficients (kL=2, k1=0.048, k2=0.014). |
| `Cie94GraphicArts` | `17` | CIE94 with graphic-arts coefficients (kL=1, k1=0.045, k2=0.015). |
| `CieDe2000` | `18` | CIEDE2000 perceptual color distance. |

#### `IColorDitherer`

Color-domain ditherer contract. Operates directly on `Color`-based palettes locked through `IBitmapLocker`, so callers don't have to learn the generic `TWork`/`TPixel`/`TDecode`/`TMetric` machinery of `IDitherer`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dither` | `void Dither(IBitmapLocker source, BitmapData target, Color[] palette, Func<Color, Color, int> colorDistanceMetric = null)` | Dithers `source` into the indexed `target` against `palette`. |

#### `IColorQuantizer`

Color-domain quantizer contract. Reduces a histogram (or color set) to a fixed-size palette of `Color`s. Designed for tools that work in `Color` space (CLI converters, palette designers, GIF writers) and don't want to bind to the generic `TWork` machinery of `IQuantizer`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ReduceColorsTo` | `Color[] ReduceColorsTo(ushort numberOfColors, IEnumerable<Color> usedColors)` | Reduces `usedColors` down to at most `numberOfColors` representative colors. Each input color is treated as having weight 1. |
| `ReduceColorsTo` | `Color[] ReduceColorsTo(ushort numberOfColors, IEnumerable<ValueTuple<Color, uint>> histogram)` | Reduces a color histogram to at most `numberOfColors` representative colors. Higher-count entries influence the result more. |

#### `KMeansColorRefinementWrapper`

Wraps any `IColorQuantizer` with iterative k-means cluster reassignment over the produced palette. Each iteration assigns every histogram color to its nearest palette entry under the supplied metric, then recomputes each palette entry as the weighted centroid of its cluster. Improves perceptual quality at the cost of O(iterations × histogramSize × paletteSize) extra work.

Implements `IColorQuantizer`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KMeansColorRefinementWrapper` | `KMeansColorRefinementWrapper(IColorQuantizer inner, int iterations, Func<Color, Color, int> metric)` |  |

| `ReduceColorsTo` | `Color[] ReduceColorsTo(ushort numberOfColors, IEnumerable<ValueTuple<Color, uint>> histogram)` |  |

#### `PaletteLookup`

Color-domain analogue of `PaletteLookup`. Caches lookups so repeated probes for the same color are O(1).

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PaletteLookup` | `PaletteLookup(IEnumerable<Color> palette, Func<Color, Color, int> metric = null)` |  |

| `FindClosestColorIndex` | `int FindClosestColorIndex(Color color)` | Returns the index of the palette entry closest to `color` under the configured metric. Repeated calls for the same color hit the cache. |

#### `PcaColorQuantizerWrapper`

Wraps any `IColorQuantizer` with PCA preprocessing: rotates the input histogram into its principal-component basis, quantizes there, and rotates the resulting palette back. Useful when the histogram's color cluster is elongated along non-axis-aligned directions (e.g. a sky gradient or a sepia photograph) — the inner quantizer can split more efficiently in PCA space.

Implements `IColorQuantizer`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |

| `Apply` | `static Bitmap Apply(Bitmap source)` | Reads the EXIF orientation of `source` and returns a new bitmap re-oriented to the upright "Normal" view. |
| `Read` | `static ExifOrientationValue? Read(Bitmap source)` | Reads the EXIF orientation tag (0x0112) from `source`. |

#### `ExifOrientationValue`

EXIF orientation tag values per Exif 2.32 §4.6.4 / TIFF tag 0x0112.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Normal` | `1` | 0x01: top-left (no transform required — already upright). |
| `MirrorHorizontal` | `2` | 0x02: top-right (mirror horizontally). |
| `Rotate180` | `3` | 0x03: bottom-right (rotate 180°). |
| `MirrorVertical` | `4` | 0x04: bottom-left (mirror vertically). |
| `MirrorHorizontalRotate270` | `5` | 0x05: left-top (mirror horizontally + rotate 270° clockwise). |
| `Rotate90` | `6` | 0x06: right-top (rotate 90° clockwise). |
| `MirrorHorizontalRotate90` | `7` | 0x07: right-bottom (mirror horizontally + rotate 90° clockwise). |
| `Rotate270` | `8` | 0x08: left-bottom (rotate 270° clockwise). |

#### `IResampleKernelWithSafePath<TPixel, TWork, TKey, TDecode, TProject, TEncode>`

Optional extension interface implemented by resampler kernels that can provide an OOB-free fast path for the destination-image interior. When a kernel implements this, the pipeline splits the destination into 4 edge bands + 1 safe interior and dispatches the interior to `ResampleUnchecked` — zero per-pixel OOB branch, ready for SIMD.

Implements `IResampleKernel<TPixel, TWork, TKey, TDecode, TProject, TEncode>`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GetSafeDestinationRegion` | `Rectangle GetSafeDestinationRegion()` | Destination-pixel rectangle where every kernel sample falls inside the source image. Empty rectangle = no safe interior (kernel larger than source); pipeline falls back to the bounds-checked path for every pixel. Typically computed via `ResampleKernelHelpers.ComputeSafeDestinationRegion`. |
| `ResampleUnchecked` | `void ResampleUnchecked(NeighborFrame<TPixel, TWork, TKey, TDecode, TProject> frame, int destX, int destY, TPixel* dest, int destStride, in TEncode encoder)` | Same as `Resample` but the caller guarantees every sample sits inside the source image. Kernel implementations use `GetUnchecked` for every sample — no bounds check, no mode dispatch, no canvas fallback. |

#### `NeighborFrame<TPixel, TWork, TKey, TDecode, TProject>`

Manages a sliding 5x5 pixel window over a frame with dual-type projections.

Implements `IDisposable`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NeighborFrame` | `NeighborFrame(TPixel* sourcePtr, int width, int height, int stride, TDecode decoder, TProject projector, OutOfBoundsMode horizontalMode = 0, OutOfBoundsMode verticalMode = 0, TPixel canvasPixel = null, int startY = 0, int decodeCacheRowCount = 0)` | Creates a new NeighborFrame over the specified source. |
| `CurrentY` | `int CurrentY { get; }` | Gets the current Y position. |
| `Height` | `int Height { get; }` | Gets the height of the source frame. |
| `Item` | `NeighborPixel<TWork, TKey> this[int x, int y] { get; }` | Gets a pixel at the specified coordinates with full decode/project. Use this for random access outside the optimized 5x5 window. |
| `Width` | `int Width { get; }` | Gets the width of the source frame. |
| `Dispose` | `void Dispose()` |  |
| `GetUnchecked` | `NeighborPixel<TWork, TKey> GetUnchecked(int x, int y)` | Reads, decodes and projects a source pixel without any bounds check. Caller must guarantee `0 <= x < Width` and `0 <= y < Height`; use `IsWindowSafe` to gate calls. Aggressively inlined so kernel inner loops compile to straight-line loads. |
| `GetWindow` | `NeighborWindow<TWork, TKey> GetWindow()` | Gets a window positioned at X=0 for the current row. |
| `IsWindowSafe` | `bool IsWindowSafe(int xMin, int xMaxExcl, int yMin, int yMaxExcl)` | True when the half-open sample window `[xMin, xMaxExcl) × [yMin, yMaxExcl)` sits fully inside the source image. Kernels call this once per destination pixel and dispatch to a no-OOB inner loop on the safe path. Single branch, very well predicted (constant per row). |
| `MoveDown` | `void MoveDown()` | Advances to the next row. O(width) operation: 5 pointer rotations + 1 row load. |
| `SeekToRow` | `void SeekToRow(int y)` | Seeks to a specific row, reloading all 5 buffer rows. O(5 * width) operation. |

## 🔌 Dependencies

## ⚠️ Limitations

- `System.Drawing.Common` is supported only on Windows from .NET 6 onwards; these extensions inherit that constraint.
- The bitmap locking helpers hand out raw memory. Respect the documented lifetime of the accessors they return.
